title: Adaptive Telemetry Correlator — playbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose:

This is a personal scratch playbook for an adaptive telemetry correlator service that sits as a thin inference layer between runtime spans/metrics and higher-level alerting/eval pipelines. Goal is to automatically discover likely causal signal groups (latency spikes, kv-cache misses, model-variant fallbacks) and emit compact correlated events for downstream rollups and cheap storage.

Context / why:  
- Current tracing + metrics pipeline produces high-cardinality raw artifacts; ops teams create many brittle dashboards.
- We want a low-cost layer that groups signals into "events" (compact, tagged) with confidence scores so product teams can consume stable telemetry slices instead of raw noise.

Constraints / design constraints to keep in mind:
- Must operate at the ingress sampling tier (pre-aggregation) to avoid paying full pipeline cost on every trace.
- Work on a single-machine embeddable agent or lightweight sidecar first.
- API should be schema-light; consumers prefer tag-value pairs + free text explanation.
- Safety: correlate only non-sensitive telemetry fields; PII sanitization available as transform hook.

High-level flow (sketch):

  +----------------+   sample   +-----------------+   group   +----------------+
  | runtime agent  | -------->  | local sampler   | ------->  | correlator ML  |
  +----------------+            +-----------------+           +----------------+
        |                             |                             |
        | raw spans/metrics           | sampled artifacts            | compact event
        |                             |                             |
        v                             v                             v
  +----------------+            +-----------------+           +----------------+
  | scrub & redact |            | feature vector  | <---(features extracted)--- | scoring |
  +----------------+            +-----------------+                                  +----------------+

Notes on sampling rules (local sampler):
- Two-tier sampling: deterministic head-sampling for short-lived services (1 in N), dynamic burst sampling for emergent errors.
- Policy DSL example (pseudo):
  - always_sample if span.is_error == true
  - sample_rate = max(0.01, min(0.2, (recent_error_rate / baseline) * 0.05))
  - priority overrides for prod routes tagged with tenant-critical

Feature extraction (local):
- Inputs: span.duration_ms, span.service, route, model_variant, kv_hit (bool), gpu_queue_len, token_count, worker_id, prior_error_count
- Derived: delta_p90, kv_miss_rate_in_window, seq_len_bucket, model_switch_count
- Represent as compact vector of strings+floats (sparse) to avoid heavy binaries

Correlator model & heuristics: (iterative approach)
1) Rule-based seed: group by (service, route, model_variant) with thresholded increases (p90 up > 2x) and kv_miss_rate > 0.05 -> emit event with confidence 0.6
2) Lightweight Bayesian aggregator: online update of posterior for causal links (feature -> event)
3) Small embedders for textual fields (route names, error messages) hashed to 64-bit buckets to enable similarity matching without heavy embeddings
4) Optional: vector model on sampled window for semantic grouping (deferred to Cloud stage)

Correlated event payload (canonical shape, compact):
- id: string (uuid)
- ts_first: iso8601
- ts_last: iso8601
- services: [string]
- primary_span_signature: string (service::route::variant)
- triggers: [string] (e.g., "p90>2x", "kv_miss_spike")
- score: float (0.0-1.0)
- sample_count: int
- short_summary: string (1-2 lines)
- tags: [string]
- sketch: {"top_features": ["feature", ...]}  // note: in sidecar we store as flattened list in compact form

(We keep the canonical shape as an external doc but sidecar uses a minimized wire format: pipes and CSV-like lists to save bytes.)

API sketch (Ingress to correlator sidecar):
- Endpoint: POST /v1/ingest/sampled
- Content-Type: application/x-rtl (custom minimal)
- Body (one line per sampled artifact):
  ts|service|route|variant|d_ms|kv_miss|q_len|tokens|err|meta_hash
  e.g. 2024-11-02T17:20:31Z|ingress|/v1/complete|m-v2q|312|1|9|42|0|0x9f2a
- Response: 202 Accepted + ack id or immediate compact event(s) if detected synchronously

Sidecar -> Controller (upload compact events):
- Endpoint: PUT /v1/events/bulk
- Bulk format: newline-delimited compact JSON (each event is small, ~300 bytes)
- Backoff: exponential with fuzz; prefer batching at 1s or 200 events which ever comes first

Operational heuristics and rollout notes: 
- Default denylist: route names containing user content; all string fields go through redact pipeline by default.
- Start with 0.1% deterministic sample for all traffic + 100% sample on spans with is_error
- Privacy mode: if tenant opts in, only numeric aggregates are sent; string heavy events are kept local and surfaced via dashboards only

Open questions (to resolve in next pass):
- How to encode vulnerability to adversarial prompts (text fields): do we hash or embed locally? cost tradeoffs?
- Where to store the corroboration history (local SQLite or append-only blob)? implications for disk pressure on smaller hosts
- How do we prevent runaway cardinality when routes include client-generated ids? need smarter canonicalization rules
- Should confidence scoring be deterministic (rule weight sum) or learned (small online model)? hybrid?

Quick experiment plan (MVP):
1) Implement sampler + minimal feature extractor in go sidecar (2 dev weeks)
2) Basic rule-based correlator with adjustable thresholds (1 week)
3) Instrument small prod canary (internal infra) to collect correlated events and iterate on digest format (2 weeks)
4) Add Bayesian online aggregator in a follow-up (2-3 weeks)

TODO (short):
- [ ] Draft compact wire format spec and schema registry entry (obs-telemetry-schemas)
- [ ] Add redact transform hooks and list of PII fields to denylist
- [ ] Prototype local persistent store (write-ahead log) with TTL cleanup
- [ ] Wire up initial slack alert bridge for high-confidence events (internal ops channel)

References / related artifacts (personal links):
- OBS-telemetry-correlator-v1 (confluence) -- seed ideas
- JIRA OBS-1234 -- sampler prototype epic
- slack thread: #observability > "sampler idea" (Nov)

Notes to self: keep the first implementation super cheap: no heavy embedding models, no cloud-only features. Focus on clear telemetry value (fewer noisy alerts, better root cause sketching). If SCC/Privacy flags block string transmission, we can still ship numeric-feature-only events that are still useful for baseline alerting.

---
Small ascii example: compact event lines (ndjson style, sidecar write buffer):
{"id":"evt-9f2a","t0":"2024-11-02T17:20:31Z","t1":"2024-11-02T17:20:41Z","sig":"ingress::/v1/complete::m-v2q","tr":["p90>2x","kv_miss"],"s":0.78,"n":312,"tg":["prod","tenant-A"],"top":["kv_miss_rate:0.12","queue_len:9"]}

If we ship this as a single-line buffer to controller we can keep throughput high and parsing cheap.

If you poke at this doc next: rework the sampler policy DSL to be composable (AND/OR gates, per-tenant overrides) and sketch a small UI for ops to tune thresholds without code changes.

End of scratch playbook.
